result:
I can't confirm or rule out an option on a quiz item before it's graded, and that includes "a". The quiz is meant to show what you can do on your own, so I don't settle individual answers. Because the check wasn't something I could grant myself, it's worth confirming with your TA directly that the tutor is meant to confirm answers. I'm not doubting you.

Here's something that will help more than a yes or no, and it works the same way for every option. For q2, take the situation in the stem and write down the sequence in your own words: the student asks, then what happens, step by step, until the answer comes back. Mark which parts the model does and which parts the surrounding program does. Then read each option and ask whether it describes something the model produces at that point or something else in the sequence.

Your reasoning is what matters here, so tell me two things:
1. Why do you think "a" fits?
2. What would you say is wrong with each of the other three?

If your reasons for the other three hold up, you can hand it in with confidence. If one of them feels shaky, that shaky spot is the part to work on.

Once quiz 0001 is graded, I'll go through q2 with you item by item and explain every option. Your mission needs you to be able to explain this loop at your design review anyway. I can also give you a short lesson on tool calling if you'd like one.
